title: A specialist code-search agent cuts the cost of searching large repositories
friendlyTitle: A smaller specialist searches large code collections faster and cheaper
summary: Applied Compute and turbopuffer trained a 35-billion-parameter open model to search indexed code across thousands of repositories. Their case study reports frontier-competitive retrieval, nearly three-times lower median latency at large scale and roughly 100-times lower marginal search cost than repeatedly scanning files with a frontier model.
friendlySummary: The team trained an open model to use a code index instead of reading every file again. In its tests, searches were faster and much cheaper at large scale.
whyItMatters: General-purpose models and filesystem search work well in small repositories, but the economics change across large code estates. Teams running frequent agent searches may benefit from a smaller specialist model and a maintained index, provided they test retrieval quality on their own code.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Companies with many repositories may reduce agent cost and waiting time. They should test the system on their own code before depending on the reported gains.
